title: Ending the '69 × 71' Loop in My Daughter's Math Drills | vitalii.no
description:
My daughter's Tier-2 bonus math task kept handing her the exact same problem, 69 × 71, three days running. Each grade's question generator only had a handful of makers cycling in a fixed order, and some of their variant ranges were narrow enough that a short run of bad luck produced the literal same question over and over — it read like a bug to a kid doing the drill honestly, and it did nothing to reinforce what she was actually getting wrong.

I rewrote the question generator so every maker carries topic tags matching the nightly analyzer's own vocabulary, and widened each grade to about nine makers with bigger variant ranges — squares, powers, square roots, percent framing, arbitrary fractions, averages, missing-factor equations. A new wrapper reads a rolling list of the last 200 questions each child has actually seen and passes it in as an avoid set; a maker rerolls up to 14 times before accepting a question, so even a narrow variant space doesn't spin forever. It also routes roughly a third of every bonus set to whatever topic the nightly analyzer flagged as that child's weak spot, all stored in Supabase.

Verified offline with a property test: 36,600 generated answers checked by an independent recomputer, with zero in-set duplicates and zero cross-day repeats against the avoid set. The literal '69 × 71, three days running' complaint that started this is now structurally impossible.
